tickets.title: The inspector's three tabs, each carrying its own worst state into the always-visible strip
tickets.defect: Section 4 of docs/UI_REDESIGN_DESIGN.md specifies an inspector with three tabs -- [copier] [risk] [rare] -- and they do not exist. Everything the inspector shows is stacked on one scroll inside the right pane. That is only half a defect on its own; the dangerous half is what building tabs naively does. This page's whole value is that Inert, ConfiguredNotEvaluated and a non-acting copier are visible WITHOUT BEING LOOKED FOR, which is why section 4.2 killed top-level nav tabs and recorded the decision 'so nobody re-adds them'. Anything that puts a section behind a click must therefore carry that section's worst state into the always-visible strip. MEASURED on the deployed box 2026-08-17: GET /api/riskguard/inventory returns 97 accounts x 23 rules = 2231 rule rows, `unevaluatedRules` is EMPTY, and the state histogram is EvaluatedNotEnforcing 1129 / Inert 559 / Disabled 543. So on a box with accounts loaded, Inert is the worst state that exists, and a strip watching only unevaluatedRules renders three clean tabs over exactly the condition the page exists to make unmissable. BridgeInspectorTabs currently exists as a STUB returning empty lists, so all four acceptance tests are red on their own assertions.
tickets.spec: Implement RankOfRuleState, Build and RuleRowsFromInventory in addons/BridgeInspectorTabs.cs. RankOfRuleState ranks a guard rule's state on the SAME scale BridgeFleetView already uses -- LOWER IS WORSE -- so one comparator serves the tree and the strip; two scales in one page is two things to keep in step, and BridgeFleetView.cs's own header warns that the copier and system severities already disagree. Inert must rank WORSE than EvaluatedNotEnforcing: a rule that cannot fire is a worse answer to 'is the guard protecting me' than one that is evaluating and has not tripped. An UNRECOGNISED state must rank WORST, never best -- BridgeFleetView.RankOfSystemSeverity does exactly this and the reason is in its comment. Build returns exactly THREE tabs, always, in section 4's order (copier, risk, rare), even when every input list is empty: an absent tab and an empty one read identically to whatever renders them, which is the sixteenth mutant of slice 1's battery. Every tab must carry a non-empty Badge AND a non-empty Reason even when nothing is wrong, because a blank badge over a state nobody has looked at is the hiding hazard. Each tab's Rank is the WORST of the rows it would show, folded with BridgeFleetView.WorstOf so the empty-set answer stays the one that method already decided. The risk tab's badge must NAME the worst state and COUNT the rows in it, recomputed from ruleRows -- never a number a producer supplied. When selectedAccount is non-null the risk tab counts only that account's rows; when it is null it counts the whole fleet. The copier tab folds copierRows through the existing BridgeFleetView.RankOfCopierRow; the rare tab folds configConflicts. RuleRowsFromInventory maps the live payload: accounts[] each with accountName and rules[], each rule with name and state. Be tolerant of a missing field the way BridgeFleetView.RowsFromSnapshot is, and skip nothing silently that would change a count.
